display_name: Stop the solet (macOS drain-sentinel + detached watchdog)
description: Plugin-namespace registration that backs service_interface::self_deployment_service::stop_self when the local profile binds self_deployment_service: macos_self_deployment_plugin. Writes a single cross-color drain sentinel at ~/.ananta/runtime/<solet>.draining (the same sentinel Slice 4 introduced for blue-green drain coordination — when present, the LaunchAgent's PathState predicate evaluates to false and respawn is suppressed). Then spawns a detached Python subprocess that sleeps briefly (~0.5s — long enough for the MCP response to flush back to the caller), SIGTERMs this solet process, waits ~10s, and escalates to SIGKILL if the SIGTERM was ignored. The watchdog runs in its own POSIX session (start_new_session=True) so the SIGTERM does not cascade back. After the verb returns, the calling solet process dies; the sentinel persists on disk; the LaunchAgent observes the sentinel and does NOT respawn. Operator brings the solet back by running ./launch.py, which scrubs the sentinel via _cleanup_stale_runtime_files (Slice 4 + 4.5 wiring) and re-spawns the solet from scratch. Idempotent: if the sentinel already exists at dispatch time (a prior stop_self the operator never cleaned up), returns StopSelfStatus.ALREADY_STOPPED without re-spawning a watchdog. The reason argument is required. Omitting dry_run performs no action; dry_run=True plans + reports the would-be sentinel path and watchdog parameters without writing the sentinel or spawning the subprocess. Malformed dry_run values are refused before any sentinel write or watchdog spawn.
embedding_description: Stop the solet on macOS and leave it stopped: write the draining sentinel so the LaunchAgent keeps it down, then terminate the running process. Returns before termination fires so the caller's response flushes first. Bringing it back is a manual launch, which clears the sentinel. Idempotent when it is already stopped.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Stop the solet queued (drain sentinel + detached watchdog spawned)
result_processor_customizations.result_description: StopSelfResult envelope with status (success / already_stopped / failed / dry_run), reason echo, duration_seconds (sub-second on macOS — the watchdog runs out-of-process), stopped_at (ISO-8601 UTC of the watchdog spawn moment), backend_action_id (the spawned watchdog pid as a string — operator can `ps` to confirm), dry_run echo, message describing the sentinel path + watchdog parameters.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: When status='success', surface the backend_action_id (watchdog pid) so the operator can `ps -p <pid>` to confirm the watchdog is queued, plus the stopped_at timestamp. When status='already_stopped', surface that the sentinel was already on disk — the operator likely ran stop_self earlier and never cleaned it up by running ./launch.py. When status='dry_run', surface the would-be sentinel path so the operator can confirm where it would have landed. When status='failed', surface the message verbatim — filesystem errors writing the sentinel or subprocess.Popen errors spawning the watchdog.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Stop the solet on macOS without restart.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_args: stop_self requires a non-empty reason. failed: sentinel write or watchdog spawn raised an exception — check the message for the underlying OSError / subprocess error.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: missing_args: re-invoke with a non-empty reason string. failed (sentinel write): check permissions on ~/.ananta/runtime/ + disk space; the directory should exist with mode 0700. failed (watchdog spawn): check sys.executable resolves to a working Python interpreter.
